svg.text: Enterprise trust ladder
Same three gates, mapped to the enterprise director relationship
COLD CONTACT
They don't know you yet
Make yourself useful before asking. Share a relevant insight.
PILOT DEAL / SMALL TEST
The Mitsui gate: they gave you a small order
Most important moment. Meet terms exactly. One failure resets to zero.
REPEAT ENGAGEMENT
They came back. Character tests are running.
Do you deliver bad news proactively? Treat their junior team well?
TRUSTED VENDOR
Reliable but interchangeable. Still a line item.
Where most companies get stuck permanently. Comfortable plateau.
STRATEGIC PARTNER
They ask what you think before deciding.
You see real problems, not scope documents. They defend you to procurement.
Pilot deal response protocol
Delivery is 40% of evaluation. Process is the other 60%.
1. Over-deliver on scope, under-deliver on drama
10-15% more than scoped, quietly. Don't invoice for extra. The pilot is seed-planting.
2. Communicate like a partner, not a vendor
Proactive updates before being asked. Share intel outside scope.
3. Surface problems early, with a proposed solution
"This timeline is at risk, here is why, here is what I recommend."
4. Deliver the insight, not just the output
Noticed a scaling problem during the work? Tell them. That's the partner move.
5. Follow up with the nemawashi debrief
"What worked, what didn't, what would you want different?" Then incorporate visibly.
Enterprise anti-patterns that keep you a vendor forever
Optimizing for the invoice / Telling them what they want to hear / Only talking to your buyer
Disappearing between engagements / Surprising them in front of their people
